Question: Three non-overlapping regular plane polygons, at least two of which are congruent, all have sides of length \(1.\) The polygons meet at a point \(A\) in such a way that the sum of the three interior angles at \(A\) is \(360^\circ.\) Thus the three polygons form a new polygon with \(A\) as an interior point. What is the largest possible perimeter that this polygon can have?
